title: holon audit regress reports 680 'NOT covered' M3 hash changes that are artifacts of diffing against the previous commit in log order, not the commit's parent
reproduction: `python -m holon audit regress --from 2b4578afc7bb71c19715c1df680c824b218bd4ec --to c3eda1976c6811ff181fd71ae6ad1166f7e86a49 --json` (audit/rounds/M3/round2/a3_summary.json): 1126 hash changes, 680 with covered_by [], exactly 136 laws (every M3 law of round 1) at each of 38d66f5, 4f0f51b, ecbb695, 41c7e34 (merges) and 1214153, as A->B->A toggles. hash_changes walks `git log A..B -- <law>` and compares each version with the previous one in that list (holon/audit/regress.py hash_changes, prev), which on merged histories is often a commit of the other branch. Against the actual parents, none is an uncovered change: at 41c7e34 and ecbb695 the registry hash equals the first parent's; at 38d66f5 and 4f0f51b the change against the first parent carries a catalog_rederivation or hash_migration line with exactly those two hashes (135 laws), and the remaining law (L_pinit_Rollup_importGenesisBatch_committedBatches_17_9) is absent from the first parent and equal to the second; at 1214153 (one parent) the change against the parent has a hashed line. The real uncovered set at the target is empty, but the report a human reads says 680.
plan_or_paper_ref: whitepaper §9.5 A3; holon/audit/regress.py; holon.statement_diff.registry_changes (G2 compares against parents)
suggested_fix: In hash_changes, compare each commit's version with its parents' versions (as statement_diff.registry_changes does), not with the previous commit in log order.
